standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Same chapter, the lemmas describing constructible sheaves of the three kinds as the finitely generated objects built from the representable sheaves and the n-torsion extension sheaves

standard_prerequisites.name: Sections commute with filtered colimits
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Sites, the lemma computing sections of a filtered colimit of sheaves as the filtered colimit of the sections
standard_prerequisites.use: Supplies the identity Mor(h_U, colim G_i) = colim Mor(h_U, G_i) used in the set case.

core_obligations: Set case (proof lines 12511-12517): by the structure lemma it suffices to prove the statement for h_U with U quasi-compact and quasi-separated; since Mor(h_U, G) = G(U), the result is the statement that sections commute with filtered colimits.

Abelian and module cases (proof lines 12519-12525): the same argument applies using the corresponding structure lemmas, with the extra observation that for an abelian sheaf Mor(j_{U!}Z/nZ, G) is the n-torsion subgroup of G(U).
proof_roadmap: Reduce to representable sheaves in the set case and use commutation of sections with filtered colimits.
Repeat the argument with the structure lemmas for abelian sheaves and modules, noting the n-torsion description.
difficulty_reason: The lemma states that constructible sheaves of sets, abelian groups or Lambda-modules are compact with respect to filtered colimits (statement lines 12496-12508). The proof (proof lines 12510-12525) reduces to the representable or n-torsion generators supplied by the structure lemmas and uses the commutation of sections with filtered colimits, with the additional identification of the Hom group out of j_{U!}Z/nZ as n-torsion. H2: one reduction applied to three cases, written out.
